title: White Australia Policy
summary: The Immigration Restriction Act became law on 23 December 1901, among the first measures of Australia's new federal parliament. It aimed to limit non-British migration and let officers impose a 50-word dictation test, which formally established the White Australia policy. The test ended in 1958 and the policy was eased from March 1966.

uncertainty.note: Start is the Act's commencement as law; end is when restrictions were announced as eased (March 1966), not a clean end of all effects.
